document.title: UK adaptation: the gap between risk and delivery
document.subtitle: Progress in adapting to climate change – 2025 report to Parliament
document.purpose: Compress the CCC's 170-page progress assessment into the central risk, delivery gap and four areas for government action.
document.core_question: Is the UK adapting at the pace required by the climate risks it already faces?

editorial_policy.notes: The long report is reorganized around the executive assessment: rising hazards, inadequate delivery and the four programme-level actions recommended by the CCC.

design_system.notes: CCC purple identity retained; complex assessment tables are compressed into decision-focused scenes.

evidence.text: The increasing impacts of climate change are clear; adaptation is needed now for current extreme weather and the rapidly increasing severity of future risks.

The world temporarily exceeded 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels in 2024; further climate change will bring the UK rising sea levels, warmer and wetter winters, and drier and hotter summers with more intense heatwaves and localised extreme rainfall.
Over a third of UK railway and road kilometres are currently at flood risk, predicted to rise to around half by 2050.
The CCC finds inadequate overall progress on delivering adaptation outcomes: no outcome has evidence of 'good' delivery, and 12 of 46 outcomes are scored insufficient.
The CCC recommends four key programme-level areas of action to strengthen the national approach to climate resilience.
Improve objectives and targets with clear, measurable adaptation objectives and sectoral targets.
Improve coordination across government and better integrate adaptation and climate risk with wider resilience activity.
Integrate adaptation within relevant policies and spending decisions, with sufficient funding and clarity on roles.
Implement monitoring, evaluation and learning across sectors; almost every indicator available to track adaptation progress lacks a target.

scenes.message: Climate risk is already material; the adaptation response is not keeping pace.
scenes.title: The risk is moving faster than the response.
scenes.body: The CCC's progress report starts from impacts already being felt, then asks whether policy and delivery are changing quickly enough.

transformations.description: The executive-summary opening is compressed into a single decision frame.

scenes.message: The report ties current records to a worsening risk envelope.
scenes.title: Today's extremes are the baseline, not the endpoint.

items.text: Over a third of UK railway and road kilometres are currently at flood risk, rising to around half by 2050.

transformations.description: Two executive risk indicators are paired to connect climate trend and infrastructure exposure without creating a composite metric.

scenes.message: No assessed outcome has evidence of good delivery.
scenes.body: There is still inadequate overall progress on delivering adaptation outcomes. The CCC does not find a single outcome with evidence of 'good' delivery.

transformations.description: The core assessment is retained nearly verbatim and isolated as the central turning point.

scenes.title: Twelve assessed outcomes are scored insufficient.
scenes.body: The wider judgement is that progress is too slow, stalled or heading in the wrong direction across the available indicators.

transformations.description: The published count is retained and isolated for emphasis.

chapters.title: Four changes to the national approach

scenes.message: The CCC recommends four programme-level changes to make adaptation more effective.
scenes.title: Change the operating system of adaptation.

steps.title: Objectives & targets
steps.headline: Define what climate-resilient means
steps.text: Set clear overarching objectives and measurable sectoral targets.

steps.title: Coordination
steps.headline: Connect adaptation to wider resilience
steps.text: Strengthen coordination across departments, spending decisions and resilience activity.

steps.title: Policy & funding
steps.headline: Integrate adaptation into mainstream decisions
steps.text: Use spending and policy processes to avoid locking in risk and to resource resilience.

steps.title: Monitoring & learning
steps.headline: Measure outcomes, not just activity
steps.text: Build the indicators, targets and data collection needed to track whether adaptation is working.

transformations.description: The four programme-level recommendations are converted into a scroll sequence, preserving their distinct roles.

chapters.title: A turning point, not a progress update

scenes.message: The CCC frames the report as a turning point: rising risks are clear, delivery remains inadequate, and the national adaptation approach needs to change.
scenes.title: From tracking adaptation to driving it.

transformations.description: The close synthesises the executive urgency, delivery assessment and four programme-level actions.
